evidence: provider documentation and crit-labs' own source; calls, formats and GPUs are as the providers state them, not measured by crit unless a kernel says so

operations.what: per routed layer of a prompt chunk: the routes sorted by expert, each expert's rows times its gate/up and down matrices in their stored format with SwiGLU between, each token's expert outputs summed with its routing weights; one weight pointer per expert, wherever the expert sits
operations.verify: on the target, run the kernel and moe_block on the same 8-16 tokens of a real chunk (their routes, routing weights and expert weights, decoded with decode_matrix): the largest difference within the kernel's arithmetic (about 2% of the largest output for FP16 tiles; 4-bit activations add the quality mode's drift), the same bits on a repeat, and a token's output unchanged when its chunk is cut differently. Keep the fastest kernel that passes; drop one that fails

kernels.call: a CUTLASS 3/4 grouped GEMM with a ptr-array problem shape (cutlass::gemm::GroupProblemShape and a ptr-array kernel schedule): one problem per expert, device arrays of A, B and D pointers; the block-scaled variants also take a scale-factor pointer per expert
kernels.shapes: any rows per expert; N and K aligned as the chosen tile and the format's scale blocks require
kernels.scale_layout: block-scaled formats read scale factors in CUTLASS's interleaved scale-factor layout, not the checkpoint's row-major [rows][cols / 16]: repack them once at load
kernels.notes: fastest where the format has its own tensor cores; its rate climbs with rows per expert, which is the curve schedule.py chooses the chunk from

kernels.call: cublasGemmGroupedBatchedEx (CUDA 12.5 and newer): per-group transposes, m, n, k, alpha and beta on the host, device arrays of A, B and C pointers, one group per expert
kernels.shapes: any; 4-bit or 8-bit experts must be widened to 16 bits first, which costs their decode bandwidth

kernels.call: moe_block(x, ids, weights, fmt, gate_up_table, down_table, inter), or the ops route_sort, gather, grouped_projection, swiglu and combine
archs: NVIDIA sm_70 and newer (FP16 tensor cores via nvcuda::wmma); not HIP
kernels.shapes: projection input width a multiple of 32, output width a multiple of 64; any tokens, top-k and experts
kernels.notes: a baseline to replace: FP16 tiles for every format with the weights decoded per tile; stable route sort, no atomics, a token's result independent of its chunk-mates; not measured yet
